peer_links.note: Documented vehicle-to-vehicle and drone-to-drone link rates for the gossip (peer) path. Spec figures are physical-layer rates from the standard or vendor 'up to' figures; measured figures are field results with their test conditions. No 5G NR sidelink field-measured throughput was found (2024 to 2025 reports are interoperability tests), so NR V2X is not used. The deployed drone dock systems have no aircraft-to-aircraft data link; the drone peer rates are the radios that would have to be added.

sources: J. B. Kenney, Dedicated Short-Range Communications (DSRC) Standards in the United States, Proc. IEEE 99(7):1162-1182, 2011, doi:10.1109/JPROC.2011.2132790 (rate set on a 10 MHz channel)

R. Molina-Masegosa and J. Gozalvez, LTE-V for Sidelink 5G V2X Vehicular Communications, IEEE Veh. Technol. Mag., 2017, ieeexplore 8080373 (802.11p 'default 6Mbps data rate' and the 18 Mbps configuration)

ground_vehicle.conditions: four nodes (three vehicles, one roadside unit) sharing the channel, commercial Cohda MK6 radios, 20 MHz, MCS automatic, 20 dBm, retransmission on, iperf UDP offered load 5 Mbps per client; the peak is read from the throughput trace figure, so it is approximate; the offered-load cap makes these lower bounds on link capacity
sources: B. Wu et al., CooperScene: Multi-Modal Cooperative Autonomy Benchmark with C-V2X Communication Characterization, Univ. of California Riverside, arXiv:2606.31219, 2026 (Table 6: 0.72 Mbps; Fig. 5: peak about 2.6 Mbps; Tables 7 and 8 and Appendix B.2 for the radio configuration)

consumer_vehicle_update_practice.source: Tesla Model 3 owner's manual, Software Updates page, read 2026-10-08
quotes: In most cases, your vehicle must be connected to Wi-Fi to download the software update.
Although you can drive while the software update is being downloaded, doing so can interrupt the download if your vehicle loses the Wi-Fi connection.
You CANNOT drive while software is being installed.
On an as-needed basis, Tesla also sends software updates using a cellular connection.
Some software updates take approximately 30 minutes to complete (some may take longer). Model 3 must be in Park while the software is being updated.
When Automatically Install Updates is enabled, your vehicle will download updates automatically and install them at 2 a.m. as long as: Model 3 is parked at the location you have set as Home.
consumer_vehicle_update_practice.reading: A consumer vehicle has a de facto depot (home Wi-Fi) and a nightly window; the download is window-gated by Wi-Fi presence and resumable, the install is atomic. What the consumer class lacks is redeployment control, not a window.
